sections.html:
Everything runs out of 100 West Franklin in Clinton, ZIP 64735. The assessor, at 660-885-7212, opens early: 7:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on weekdays, with evening or weekend visits by appointment. The assessor's page also links the county GIS map.

The bill itself comes from the Henry County Treasurer, who doubles as Ex Officio Collector of Revenue. Reach that desk at 660-885-7207, by fax at 660-885-7259 or at collector@henrycountymo.net. A question about worth belongs to the assessor, and a question about what you owe belongs to the collector.

sections.h2: Housing and land in Henry County
sections.html:
West-central Missouri's Henry County counts 22,671 residents and 10,750 housing units, with Clinton as the seat and biggest town. Owners occupy 75.0 percent of homes, and the median owned home is valued at $160,600. Carrying a mortgage costs about $1,212 a month, median rent is $768 and median household income is $57,926. Builders took out just 18 permits in 2025, so most buyers are shopping resale.

Hilly timber and creek ground near the Truman Reservoir draws hunters and anglers. A shoreline or wooded parcel gets marketed differently from a Clinton or Windsor town lot, and its assessment class can differ too, since farmland and residential ground carry different rates. Buyers also ask about the school district, which the assessor's parcel record shows.

A home is taxed on 19 percent of its market value, farmland on 12 percent and commercial property on 32 percent (RSMo 137.115). Odd-numbered years bring new values, and they hold through the following even year.

  • A home value that rises over 15 percent, excluding new construction, needs an inspection on site.
  • The owner gets written notice and at least 30 days to request an interior look.
  • Driving past the house does not meet the statute.

When an increase of that size is appealed, RSMo 138.060 makes the assessor show the value is no higher than market value.

sections.h2: Appealing a value, step by step
sections.html:
1. Pull your parcel record and check the acreage, buildings and classification against the house.
  2. Phone 660-885-7212, ask how the number was reached and offer sale prices of similar properties.
  3. If the call settles nothing, file with the Board of Equalization by the second Monday in July.
  4. If the Board's letter goes against you, take it to the State Tax Commission within 30 days of the letter. File online, email Legal@stc.mo.gov, or mail PO Box 146, Jefferson City, MO 65102-0146.
  5. Keep paying on time. A late bill draws a penalty no matter what an appeal says.

A company, trust or estate must use a lawyer to file. Send the tax bill or the Board letter first and hold the rest of your evidence. An agreed value signed with the assessor shuts the door on further appeals, so read any such paper twice before signing. The local forms are available at 660-885-7212.

Missouri taxes whoever holds the property on January 1, so dates near that day matter to a seller.

Henry County property tax dates
WhenWhat happens
January 1Assessment date
Odd yearsNew real estate values
Second Monday in JulyBoard of Equalization filing cutoff
December 31Bill due; mailed payments judged by postmark under RSMo 139.100
After January 1Collector adds penalty
Fourth Monday in AugustSale of delinquent land

Ask the collector for this year's mailing date and the penalty figure.

A seller who closes in March is still the person the county looked to for that year's assessment. The sales contract is what divides the year: either the buyer repays the seller for the months after closing or the seller credits the buyer for the months before. The county does not do that arithmetic.

Have the title company walk you through the proration clause and say which tax year it covers. Then phone the collector and ask whether any earlier year remains open. A prior-year balance is the usual snag that holds up a closing.

sections.h2: Back taxes and the August sale
sections.html:
Delinquent land can be sold on the fourth Monday of August. RSMo 140.150 allows an owner to halt the sale by paying tax, penalty, interest and costs to the collector first. First class mail carries the notice to the recorded owner, and a missing letter changes nothing.

Ask 660-885-7207 for a payoff before listing, then pass the figure to your title company. If you dispute the value, RSMo 139.031 permits payment under protest: the full amount before delinquency, a written statement to the collector and a circuit court suit within ninety days.

A house with unpaid years, an inherited title or tenants can still sell. A cash buyer needs no lender appraisal, and the tax payoff is taken from your proceeds at closing, so the county balance does not stall the deal.

sections.h2: A sale timeline that avoids tax surprises
sections.html:
Work backward from your closing date. Four to six weeks out, request the payoff and the parcel record. Two weeks out, confirm with the collector that no prior year has been added or left open. At the closing table, the title company pays the collector from your proceeds and splits the current year as the contract directs.

If you list in the fall, remember that bills are mailed around then and come due December 31. If you list in the spring, the January 1 assessment already belongs to you as the holder, so the contract should say how the buyer will repay your share. A buyer who closes after the due date inherits nothing from you except what the contract assigns, but a lien for unpaid tax follows the land, so a clear payoff letter matters more than any promise.

When the house is vacant, inherited or rented to a tenant, the same steps apply. Pay what is owed, get the receipt, and keep it with the closing papers.

sections.h2: Papers worth gathering before you list
sections.html:
Keep the assessor's parcel record, the collector's current balance and any notice about a changed value in one folder. A buyer's agent will ask what the land is classed as, what the bill is and whether anything is overdue, and those three papers answer all of it.

If your value jumped, note the notice date and remember that the Board window shuts on the second Monday in July. Calling the assessor early in the week leaves room to fix a problem before a closing date.

faqs.q: Who prints the Henry County property tax bill?
faqs.a: The Treasurer, acting as Ex Officio Collector of Revenue, at 100 West Franklin in Clinton. Phone 660-885-7207.

faqs.q: Which percentage applies to a Henry County home?
faqs.a: Nineteen percent of true value, against 12 percent for farmland and 32 percent for commercial property. The local levy then applies to that assessed figure.

faqs.q: Is there a grace period after December 31?
faqs.a: A mailed payment is judged by its postmark, and the collector adds a penalty starting January 1. Ask the collector's office whether an exception applies to you.

faqs.q: Could the county sell my home over unpaid tax?
faqs.a: Yes, delinquent land can be sold on the fourth Monday of August. Paying the tax, penalty, interest and costs before then stops it.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Henry County assessor?
faqs.a: Call 660-885-7212 or visit 100 West Franklin in Clinton, weekdays 7:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Appointments outside those hours are available.
